## TL;DR

The phone task-detail tab strip now wraps onto two rows at 390px and three rows at 320px, so all seven tabs plus the expand control are visible and tappable instead of scrolling off-screen. Preview guidance copy now gets a full-width line capped at 52ch instead of being squeezed beside the target selector and Start preview button. Desktop is untouched: the wrap only applies inside the existing `max-width: 719.98px` block, while the single scrolling row remains the behaviour above it. I verified the layout with a headless Chromium measurement against the real stylesheet at both widths and both themes, and `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed.

## Work and rationale

The task followed #1137, which made the task drawer one shared mobile detail but solved the seven-tab overflow by adding `drawer-tabs-scroll` — horizontal scrolling below 720px. That made tabs technically reachable but still hid the right-hand tabs (and the fullscreen control) with no visual affordance that more existed. #1147's acceptance criterion is stronger: at 390px and 320px every tab must be reachable without accidental clipping. Scrolling still leaves destinations off-screen, so I changed the phone presentation rather than tuning the scroll.

The tab fix is CSS-only and deliberately scoped to the existing phone media query. At `< 720px`, `.drawer-tabs-scroll` now sets `flex-wrap: wrap` and `overflow-x: visible`. The existing `.drawer-tabs-scroll .tab-btn` rules still give each button `flex: none` and `white-space: nowrap`, so labels never split mid-word, and the #1137 `min-height: 44px` touch floor is preserved. The fullscreen control keeps its `margin-left: auto`, so it lands at the right edge of the final row. No template markup changed; I only updated the stale comment in `TaskDrawer.vue` that described the strip as horizontal scrolling.

The preview copy fix addresses a different squeeze. `.quickbar-row > :first-child { flex: 1; min-width: 0 }` let the first helper paragraph -- "Choose which preview target to serve." or "No preview running." -- share the row with the target select and Start preview, leaving it one or two words wide. Inside the phone query, `.quickbar-row > .preview-hint` now takes `flex: 1 1 100%`, `min-width: 0` and `max-width: 52ch`. The higher-specificity selector overrides the generic first-child rule, and the 100% flex basis forces the controls below. The secondary platform note ("Runs on this control-plane host...") gets the same treatment because it is also a direct `.quickbar-row > .preview-hint` child. I kept that note rather than deleting it: it carries real information about remote runners, and wrapping satisfies the acceptance criterion.

The mobile wrap applies to any shared `drawer-tabs-scroll` consumer at phone widths, which includes the story panel. That is consistent with the intent -- every destination visible on a phone -- and desktop behaviour for those panels is unchanged.

## Approaches tried

I first considered keeping horizontal scrolling and adding discoverability: an edge fade, a scroll hint, or `scroll-snap`. I rejected this because the tabs would still be off-screen; it improves affordance but not the acceptance criterion, and it would require extra markup or pseudo-elements to look intentional.

I considered an overflow "More" menu that collapses the trailing tabs. That hides the same destinations behind a tap, adds JavaScript state, and duplicates the mobile More sheet pattern for only four extra buttons. Seven fixed tabs are predictable and cheap to show.

I considered shrinking padding or font size to force one row. At 320px the seven labels plus icons plus the expand control cannot fit while respecting the 44px touch target floor established in #1137/#1139, so that route would fail accessibility to satisfy a cosmetic constraint.

Wrapping follows the existing precedent for the Agents sub-tabs (#1139), which already wrap below 900px. It reuses the same shared classes and needs no new component.

For the preview helper, I first tried giving the paragraph a sensible `min-width`. It still shared the row with the select and button, so it remained cramped at 390px. Forcing a full-width basis was the only arrangement that reliably produced a readable measure. I also considered removing "No preview running." as redundant next to the Start preview button; I kept it because the row can otherwise be ambiguous, and wrapping removed the harm.

## Challenges and blockers

The first repository-wide grep I ran resolved against the main checkout rather than this worktree. I stopped using relative paths for content searches and used absolute worktree paths for every subsequent read and edit.

The 320px case is inherently three rows; there is no single-row arrangement that keeps 44px targets. Three rows consume roughly 132px of vertical space, which is acceptable above the task body and far better than hidden tabs. I documented that trade-off rather than hiding it.

A direct `bunx vitest run <file>` failed because the Vue SFC plugin is only configured through the UI app's Vite config. Running the repository's wrapper, `bun run test <file>`, picked up the correct config and executed the suite.

The scoped `repoos check` reported the full test suite as skipped because the environment marked it as already running on the remote validation runner. I compensated by running the affected UI test file locally, then relied on the scoped check for build, CSS layering, theme contrast, rendered contrast, and the UI smoke test.

Finally, I did not request a managed preview. Instead I rendered mock drawer markup with the real `style.css` in headless Chromium at 390 and 320 in both themes. That measured: no strip overflow, two rows at 390 and three at 320, hint widths of 343px and 287px, at most two lines, and helper copy always above the Start preview button. The mock omits the real header and fonts, so it validates the wrap mechanics rather than pixel-identical typography; the declared review shots remain the authoritative visual evidence.

## Key learnings

"Reachable" and "discoverable" are different bars. Horizontal scrolling can satisfy the first but fails a phone review when the last destinations have no affordance, so wrapping is the stronger pattern for a small, fixed set of tabs.

When a shared flex row squeezes one child, the fix belongs on that child's selector specificity, not on the row. The generic `> :first-child { flex: 1 }` rule was the direct cause of the one-word preview lines, and a more specific rule overrides it without disturbing the running-preview row where the first child is the live URL.

Layout CSS can be validated without a preview server by combining the real stylesheet with representative markup in a headless browser. That keeps preview ownership with the human while still producing measurements for the acceptance criteria.

Scope discipline mattered here: #1145 owns the header title and alignment, so the change stayed inside the tab strip and preview row plus the CSS guard tests.
